title: Dataset catalog, partition and immutable upload batch
description: The catalog is a server-owned registry: a caller names a dataset by its public name and the core resolves the storage key, partition layout and authorization scope itself. No caller supplies an object path, bucket, SQL or a filesystem location. An upload batch is immutable: its identity is server-assigned and its key digest covers content, so the same logical batch re-announced is a duplicate ack, never a rewrite.

partitionKey.description: Server-computed path segment. Public callers see it in results but never send it.

objectKey.description: Server-computed storage key. Returned for operator diagnostics only; it is not an accepted request field anywhere.

name.description: Public dataset name. The only dataset identifier a caller may send.

authorizationScope.description: Scope a caller must hold to read this dataset. Server-side only: a request that names a different scope is rejected, not filtered.

batchID.description: Server-assigned immutable batch identity. A caller that re-announces a batch sends this value back; it never mints one.

keyDigest.description: sha256 over the canonical batch descriptor. Two announcements of the same logical batch produce the same digest and therefore one batch. Opaque to public callers.

objectDigest.description: sha256 of the uploaded object content, when the object has already been stored. Absent until then.

state.description: pending: announced, no object yet. uploaded: object stored and digest verified. committed: cataloged and queryable, terminal. abandoned: expired pending, terminal.

expiresAt.description: Pending batches are bounded in time; an expired pending batch becomes abandoned and releases its slot.
